title: Algoritmus nejkratší cesty, který vznikl za dvacet minut v kavárně
content:
Dnes pomocí něj navigace počítá nejkratší trasu. Nizozemský informatik Edsger Dijkstra ho vymyslel roku 1956 v Amsterdamu a podle vlastních slov na to potřeboval asi dvacet minut.

Seděl údajně na kavárenské terase s přítelkyní a přemýšlel, jak předvést možnosti nového počítače. Napadlo ho najít nejkratší cestu mezi dvěma městy.

Postup funguje tak, že z výchozího místa postupně prozkoumává nejbližší dosud nenavštívené uzly a u každého si pamatuje dosud nejkratší nalezenou cestu. Publikoval ho v roce 1959.

Dijkstra později říkal, že algoritmus byl jednoduchý i proto, že ho vymýšlel bez tužky a papíru. Takto vzniklý nástroj se používá v počítačových sítích i v mapových aplikacích.

A simple explanatory contrast or interaction is welcome when understood at a glance. If explanation would require many separate objects, several steps or arrows tracing which part implies the next, choose one recognizable aspect instead. Examples: a moving ambulance for Doppler effect; a book with a prohibition sign for a banned novel; a pulsar with a simple beam, without Earth, waveform, magnetic field or observation equipment. Metadata is context, not a checklist of objects to draw. Omit secondary subjects and explanatory marks when the main motif already works. Choose between a simple accompanying subject and a simple explanatory relationship according to context. A compact comparison or a useful single arrow is fine; avoid multistep experiments, networks of implications and inventories of disconnected scientific components. A small supporting symbol is welcome when immediately readable. Broad clean silhouettes, aim for 5-8 large flat shapes, at most 3 muted foreground colors and at least one third empty transparent space. Recognizable at 160x90 and clean at 320x180. Optically center the complete main motif in the full canvas with balanced transparent margins; do not reserve an empty text column. Use off-center placement only when necessary for the specific meaning, interaction or direction of action. Centering does not require mirrored or rigidly symmetric objects. At most one flat shadow plane; no realistic lighting, reflections, grain, fine textures, tiny repeated details, decorative scenery, 3D or photorealism. Preserve factual identity and avoid visible contradictions, but leave qualifications and explanations to the article. Default to no text; never add a caption merely naming the pictured object. No legends, axes, connectors or numerical readouts just for completeness. Restrained grown-up magazine artwork. Genuinely transparent background: no backdrop rectangle, black or near-black fill, dark gradient, vignette, decorative glow, border or edge color. Empty areas and corners must be transparent so the card shows through. Preserve alpha. If transparency is technically impossible, use only the supplied exact uniform fallback color. Soft translucent forms are allowed when the selected subject is light or mist, never as a backdrop.
